findings.description: The bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so objects are not explicitly protected with a customer-managed or service-managed encryption key at rest.
The bucket defines a private ACL but no default server-side encryption configuration. Ledger exports can therefore be stored without an explicitly enforced encryption-at-rest policy.

The bucket enables versioning and access logging but does not configure default server-side encryption. Model artifacts uploaded without an encryption header are not explicitly guaranteed to be encrypted at rest.
The bucket lacks a server-side encryption configuration, leaving runbook contents without explicitly enforced encryption at rest.

The object upload does not set server-side encryption or a KMS key, and its destination bucket has no default encryption configuration. The vendor roster may therefore be stored without explicitly enforced encryption at rest.
